items.title: Unable to select Sharing Only user when setting up file sharing
items.x_text:
❓ Unable to select Sharing Only user when setting up file sharing

✅ Create and modify the Sharing Only user via Terminal commands.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZkoEHvG3GI8
#COSMOS #macos

discovery.short_answer: Create and modify the Sharing Only user via Terminal commands.
discovery.full_answer: The issue of not being able to select a Sharing Only user for file sharing can be resolved by manually creating and configuring the user through Terminal. This involves creating a home directory for the user, changing ownership, and adjusting user shell and home directory settings using 'dscl' commands. After these changes, you can log in as the Sharing Only user via 'su' to verify the setup. Once confirmed, the user will appear in the Windows File Sharing list. After enabling sharing, you can revert the changes to restore the user to the original Sharing Only state. This process addresses the problem where the user does not initially appear in the sharing list and removes duplicate entries after a reboot.
discovery.grok_perspective: Users should verify any file-sharing configuration steps against official system documentation, as interface limitations may stem from version-specific restrictions or account setup variations rather than simple workarounds.

items.title: Rescuing an emulsion dressing?
items.x_text:
❓ Rescuing an emulsion dressing?

✅ Create a new emulsion with egg yolk and slowly add the broken sauce.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fMycipfXhko
#COSMOS #emulsion

discovery.short_answer: Create a new emulsion with egg yolk and slowly add the broken sauce.
discovery.full_answer: When an oil-in-water emulsion breaks and turns into a water-in-oil emulsion, it cannot be reversed by simply mixing. To rescue the dressing, you need to start a new oil-in-water emulsion. This is done by mixing a small amount of raw or pasteurized egg yolk with some water until it is well blended. Then, while the blender is running, slowly pour the separated sauce into this new mixture. If the sauce begins to separate again, shake it before continuing to add it. This method helps to re-establish the proper emulsion and salvage the dressing.
discovery.grok_perspective: Unverified online guidance on fixing separated dressings merits skepticism, since success hinges on unmentioned variables like exact ratios, temperatures, and freshness that can render attempts unreliable.

items.title: What type of parasite causes a woody flower-like growth in tree branches?
items.x_text:
❓ What type of parasite causes a woody flower-like growth in tree branches?

✅ Parasitic plants from the mistletoe family cause woody flower-like growths.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6O684Xc-Nz4
#COSMOS #botany

discovery.short_answer: Parasitic plants from the mistletoe family cause woody flower-like growths.
discovery.full_answer: Woody flower-like growths on tree branches, often called woodroses or burls, are caused by parasitic plants, particularly those from the mistletoe family. These parasites produce a root-like structure called a haustorium that penetrates the host tree's tissues to extract nutrients. The tree reacts by forming a woody outgrowth around this intrusion. The seeds of these parasitic plants are spread by fruit-eating birds, which deposit them on tree branches where they germinate. Such growths are common in regions like Indonesia and parts of Africa, where they are collected for ornamental use. Examples of parasitic plants involved include Pedistylis galpinii and Erianthemum dregei, which infect host trees such as Sclerocarya birrea and Chinaberry. The resulting woodrose varies in color depending on the host tree species.
discovery.grok_perspective: Descriptions of unusual tree growths from online sources may not capture all possible causes or variations. Direct examination by experts remains the most reliable approach for identification.

items.title: How to calculate baker s percentages for indirect doughs?
items.x_text:
❓ How to calculate baker s percentages for indirect doughs?

✅ Calculate baker's percentages either including or excluding starter flour.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dUH_xYIzdFI
#COSMOS #baking

discovery.short_answer: Calculate baker's percentages either including or excluding starter flour.
discovery.full_answer: When calculating baker's percentages for indirect doughs, such as those using a starter or preferment, there are two common approaches. One method excludes the flour contained in the starter from the total flour calculation, which is the approach used by Jeffrey Hamelman in his book 'Bread.' The other method includes the starter's flour as part of the total flour, resulting in an overall baker's percentage. Both methods are acceptable, but to avoid confusion when communicating recipes, it is recommended to clearly state which approach is being used. King Arthur Baking's resources confirm this flexibility and suggest that excluding the starter's flour is more typical, but including it provides a comprehensive percentage. Therefore, the choice depends on preference and clarity in recipe sharing.
discovery.grok_perspective: Methods for baker's percentages in indirect doughs may vary by recipe conventions, with potential inconsistencies in how fermentation components are treated. This leaves room for differing interpretations without a single standard approach.

items.title: When tiling a walk in-shower, how can I ensure the linear drain doesn t protude above the tiles?
items.x_text:
❓ When tiling a walk in-shower, how can I ensure the linear drain doesn t protude above the tiles?

✅ Use a 10mm notched trowel for thinset to match tile and drain height.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FxkS87BGUfI
#COSMOS #shower

discovery.short_answer: Use a 10mm notched trowel for thinset to match tile and drain height.
discovery.full_answer: To prevent a linear drain from protruding above the tiles in a walk-in shower, consider the thickness of your tiles and the thinset mortar layer. If your tiles are about 9mm thick and relatively large, using a thinset trowel with large notches, such as a 10mm notched trowel, will help achieve a finished thinset thickness of approximately 6 to 8mm. This thickness allows the thinset to properly bed the tiles and align the tile surface flush with the drain, avoiding any protrusion. The size of the trowel notches directly influences the thinset thickness, so selecting the appropriate notch size is key to ensuring the drain sits level with the tile surface.
discovery.grok_perspective: Tile and drain heights vary by product, so confirming compatibility through direct measurement before installation is prudent. Professional guidance may be warranted for site-specific conditions.
